reason: The event is real but the signal does not clear the desk's 70/100 bar, so no case was built. Verified: AMI Labs (Paris, founded December 2025 by Yann LeCun) announced a $1.03B seed round at a $3.5B pre-money valuation on 9-10 March 2026 (TechCrunch 9 Mar, Bloomberg 10 Mar), co-led by Cathay Innovation, Greycroft, Hiro Capital, HV Capital and Bezos Expeditions, with NVIDIA, Temasek, Samsung and Toyota Ventures among participants. The thin row's details were inaccurate: the round was a seed round, not an 'institutional funding round'; it was announced on 9-10 March, not 13 March; and Yann LeCun's title is Executive Chairman (founder), not 'Co-Founder / Chief AI Scientist' — the CEO is Alexandre LeBrun, with Laurent Solly (ex-Meta VP Europe) as COO. Honest score: capacity 18 (cash-rich), timing 12 (57 days old, no window), brand fit 9, urgency 7, ops fit 9 = 55/100 (WARM). What holds it back: a four-month-old research laboratory with no product (first partner is Nabla, a digital-health startup; stated targets are healthcare, robotics, wearables and industrial automation), no revenue, no marketing function and no stated brand motive; a sponsorship would be a talent-recruitment halo only. World models for physical systems could in principle feed race simulation, but nothing deployable exists to point at and no team-side workstream can be named without inventing it. No F1 or Formula E partner conflict exists (no AMI Labs partnership with any team or with Renault/Alpine/Stellantis found). Leadership ties: none found. Revisit only if AMI Labs ships a product for physical-systems simulation, names a commercial lead, or a French works team (Citroën Racing in FE, Alpine in F1) goes public with an AI-model need — then a French sovereign-AI flagship on a French team becomes a real case.
